summary.problem:
Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for tha

summary.problem:
Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for tha

summary.problem:
Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for tha

payload.message:
Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for that run. A follow-up rerun clears the printed backend as well.

Without the sibling edit, A→B→A can keep UI and backend aligned at `"input 2"`. Either interpretation of leftover keys should keep UI and printed state in sync; the #3512 unmount rule for an already-registered `persist_state=None` widget is that both sides reset in the same run.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: current develop / #17106
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright)

### Additional Information

Found during QA of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17106#issuecomment-5813147965.

Related:

- #3512 — unmount should reset both the widget UI and the Python value in the same run
- #17093 / #17106 — delayed first mount after a leftover pre-registration user key (out of scope here)
- #12880 — identity-by-key (out of scope)

summary.problem:
Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

# comp.py

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"

streamlit v 1.55

I'm trying to migrate our custom js widgets from v1 component api to the non-iframe v2 api.
It seems far more powerful, and seems like it'll cut boilerplate.
In our style, we have accumulated over the years a collection of js/client side running code, that doesn't particularly need/have an html or user-interfacing component.

I think I've noticed an issue, where values are getting returned from the js frontend (as seen by console.log msgs), but the streamlit backend logs see those msgs as dropped. I'm still getting the hang of the runtime behaviors of this new component api, to figure out how to update our v1 components, so I've been trying to test it. If this is not the expected or correct usage, I'm all ears, but I'm working my best from the online docs + repo src implementation. 

This is our current design / usage analysis of the v2 api:
- We declare/write a st.components.v2.component(...) object in a helper file, that will not be modified, with a unique name
- The js string includes all helper functions, and an `export default function(component: FrontendRendererArgs)`
- This default function is the per-widget-instantiation, and only run once (see below)
- It sets up callbacks or such on html elements
- If the component is called with a `key`, then all setTriggerValue and setStateValue items populate session_state
- Without an explicit `key`, setTriggerValue won't populate session_state, but the rest of the python arguments (data) are used to calculate a unique frontend key
- No two component instances therefore can have the exact same args (data)
- If the args to the component don't change, the widget object stays created, and is not re-instantiated
- If the rest of the args (data) to the component change, without a `key`, the old widget is discarded, and a new component is instantiated

Our goal is to have high-level code that uses caching & post processing of raw lower-level data call these low-level components as needed. But if the components are called, I expect them to behave consistently. 

In this particular example, the js component does (for example!!!) a failproof cookies query on instantiation and returns it via setTriggerValue.
```js
export default function (component){  component.setTriggerValue("get_cookies", document.cookie); }
```
We wrap that `st_comp_get_cookies: st.components.v2.component` in a helper function.
```python
def get_raw_cookies():
    obj = st_comp_get_cookies(data={"_": unique_line_time()})
```
If we feed `data` a value that's unique to the line (line traceback stack), the multiple calls of the widget will be unique even if fed the same other args. It would create a new component when there's a new/unique call (args or location), otherwise only instantiated once.
If we feed `data` a value that's unique in time, then every call is a new widget instance, and the js default function runs each time.

In the v1 api, when the app first loaded, the components wouldn't always respond right away. So I'd check if the returned value was empty or not.
```python
# get_raw_cookies()
if not isisntance(obj, dict) or "get_cookies" not in obj:
    # Very first run, component mightn't be ready
    time.sleep(initial_setup_sleep)
    st.rerun()
print(f"{obj["get_cookies"]=}")
```

Given the above files, with more logging added, I noticed a very strange behavior. (This is just a heavily reduced version of our real prod code; and I only chose documents.cookies because it _can't fail_).
In the browser console, everytime the page reloaded (hard reload F5, or soft rerun from some other input), the console logged the new widget instance, the cookie fetch, and that succeeded.
But in the python logs, sometimes it worked, sometimes it did not. 
With the "rerun if fail" check, if this was the only indeterminite execution, it'd work quickly enough, and then the rest of the code would execute.
But with multiple components doing this, it suddenly became impossible for both to work at the same time.
```python
get_raw_cookies() # Sometimes reruns, ok
get_raw_cookies() # Always reruns, when the above finally works
st.header("This never runs")
assert False
```

Sorry if this was rather long winded, but I'm either uncertain I'm understanding the runtime behaviors correctly, trying not to misrepresent our goals, possibly oblivious to a better v2 design, or just unaware of what to reasonably expect from this as for behavior.

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(

        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"

### Summary

I am using st.file_uploader to upload ~3.5gb file into my streamlit dashboard. This however, results in the server getting killed.
When I inspect using btop, Upon file upload, the server starts using an astronomic amount of RAM.

```Python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a video file", type=["mp4", "mov", "avi"])
```


### Steps To Reproduce

streamlit run dashboard.py --maxUploadSize=5000

### Expected Behavior

It's probably better to stream it in chunks to disk when clicking an 'upload file' button.

### Current Behavior

The server gets killed.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: سرور هنگام آپلود فایل بزرگ حافظه زیادی مصرف می‌کند و همین باعث خرابی آن می‌شود.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: محدودیت‌های حافظه در محیط‌های داکر موجب کشته شدن سرور می‌شود.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: streamlit عملکرد خاصی برای مدیریت آپلود فایل‌های بزرگ به صورت جریانی ندارد.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

### Checklist

### Summary

I am using st.file_uploader to upload ~3.5gb file into my streamlit dashboard. This however, results in the server getting killed.
When I inspect using btop, Upon file upload, the server starts using an astronomic amount of RAM.

EDIT: I tried imposing a RAM limit by dockerizing the dashboard and settting a 4gb RAM limit, but it just gets killed in the container.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a video file", type=["mp4", "mov", "avi"])
```


### Steps To Reproduce

streamlit run dashboard.py --maxUploadSize=5000

### Expected Behavior

It's probably better to stream it in chunks to disk when clicking an 'upload file' button.

### Current Behavior

The server gets killed.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Summary

I am using st.file_uploader to upload ~3.5gb file into my streamlit dashboard. This however, results in the server getting killed.
When I inspect using btop, Upon file upload, the server starts using an astronomic amount of RAM.

EDIT: I tried imposing a RAM limit by dockerizing the dashboard and settting a 4gb RAM limit, but it just gets killed in the container.

```Python
import streamlit as st

```

streamlit run dashboard.py --maxUploadSize=5000

### Expected Behavior

It's probably better to stream it in chunks to disk when clicking an 'upload file' button.

The server gets killed.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Python version:

محدودیت: مطابق مستندات و مسائل موجود در مرجع‌ها، ویجت `file_uploader` فقط یک فایل را هر بار آپلود می‌کند و فایل‌ها در RAM نگهداری می‌شوند. حذف فایل از ویجت معمولاً باعث آزاد شدن حافظه می‌شود اما به نظر می‌رسد پاکسازی کامل در حالت معمول انجام نمی‌شود. همچنین دوبار اجرا شدن callback هنگام آپلود فایل جدید می‌تواند باعث مصرف حافظه بالاتر و باقی ماندن فایل‌ها در RAM شود. نیاز به جزئیات بیشتر درباره پیاده‌سازی داخلی و تعامل با حافظه است تا بتوان علت دقیق را تعیین کرد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: فایل‌های آپلود شده در RAM باقی می‌مانند به دلیل رفتار طبیعی ویجت `st.file_uploader` که فایل‌ها را نگهداری می‌کند تا امکان دسترسی به آنها در جلسات بعد وجود داشته باشد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: امکان پاک شدن برنامه‌ریزی شده ویجت فایل آپلودر وجود ندارد و نیازمند مکانیزم دیگری برای آزادسازی حافظه است.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: دوبار اجرا شدن callback هنگام آپلود مجدد فایل ممکن است به دلیل مکانیزم داخلی تغییر فایل در ویجت باشد که باعث افزایش مصرف حافظه می‌شود.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

sources.quote:
Please note that file uploader is a **bit problematic** because
- You can only upload one file at the time.
- You get no additional information on the file like name, size, upload time, type etc. So you
cannot distinguish the files without reading the content.
- every time you interact with any widget, the script is rerun and you risk processing or storing
the file again!
- The file uploader widget is not cleared when you clear the cache and there is no way to clear the
file uploader widget programmatically.

- You can only upload one file at the time.
- You get no additional information on the file like name, size, upload time, type etc. So you
cannot distinguish the files without reading the content. The python object id changes for each script rerun so you cannot use that either.
- every time you interact with any widget, the script is rerun and you risk processing or storing
the file again!
- The file uploader widget is not cleared when you clear the cache and there is no way to clear the
file uploader widget programmatically.

On each subsequent upload after the first upload, the `on_change` callback is called twice. My understanding is that uploading a new file also clears the existing file, triggering another callback execution. In that sense, this behavior might be a feature, not a bug. Nonetheless, this behavior can be confusing and unintuitive.

Summary

```text
Please note that file uploader is a **bit problematic** because
- You can only upload one file at the time.
- You get no additional information on the file like name, size, upload time, type etc. So you
cannot distinguish the files without reading the content.
- every time you interact with any widget, the script is rerun and you risk processing or storing
the file again!

file uploader widget programmatically.
```

محدودیت: شواهد نشان می‌دهد که ویجت `st.file_uploader` فایل را در حافظه نگه می‌دارد و مشکل مصرف بالای RAM پس از انتخاب فایل مشابه گزارش‌های شناخته شده است. این موضوع احتمالا مربوط به نحوه عملکرد ویجت و مدیریت وضعیت در استریم‌لیت است و نه خطایی که با تغییر کد کاربر قابل حل باشد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: ممکن است به دلیل پیاده‌سازی داخلی `st.file_uploader` فایل آپلود شده پس از انتخاب هنوز در حافظه باقی بماند.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: فایل آپلود شده در حافظه نگهداری می‌شود تا امکان دسترسی به محتوای آن فراهم باشد ولی حافظه آزاد نمی‌شود تا زمانی که اپ استریم‌لیت بسته شود.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: مشکل احتمالا مربوط به نحوه مدیریت حافظه و پاکسازی در پایتون و استریم‌لیت است و نه خطای مشخصی در کد کاربر.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

Please note that file uploader is a **bit problematic** because
- You can only upload one file at the time.
- You get no additional information on the file like name, size, upload time, type etc. So you
cannot distinguish the files without reading the content.
- every time you interact with any widget, the script is rerun and you risk processing or storing
the file again!
- The file uploader widget is not cleared when you clear the cache and there is no way to clear the
file uploader widget programmatically.

On each subsequent upload after the first upload, the `on_change` callback is called twice. My understanding is that uploading a new file also clears the existing file, triggering another callback execution. In that sense, this behavior might be a feature, not a bug. Nonetheless, this behavior can be confusing and unintuitive.

-------- Upload-Helper --------

def save_uploaded_file(file, folder):
os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
save_path = os.path.join(folder, file.name)

with open(save_path, "wb") as f:
    shutil.copyfileobj(file, f)

def unified_upload(device_id):

}

# Upload-Counter initialisieren
if "upload_counter" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.upload_counter = {}

if device_id not in st.session_state.upload_counter:
    st.session_state.upload_counter[device_id] = 0

# Dropdown zur Auswahl des Dokumententyps
doc_choice = st.selectbox(
    "Dokumenttyp auswählen",

    format_func=lambda x: doc_types[x]["label"],

    placeholder="Bitte auswählen...",
    key=f"doc_select_{device_id}"

if not doc_choice:
    st.info("Bitte zuerst den Dokumenttyp auswählen ⬆️")
    return

# Zielordner für Gerät & Typ

    file = st.file_uploader(
        f"{doc_types[doc_choice]['label']} hochladen",
        type=doc_types[doc_choice]["allowed_types"],
        key=file_key
    )

    title = st.text_input("Titel (optional)")
    submitted = st.form_submit_button("Speichern")

    if submitted:

            st.error("Bitte eine Datei auswählen.")
        else:
            save_path = save_uploaded_file(file, folder)

            # DB-Eintrag speichern
            conn = get_connection()
            try:
                conn.execute(
                    """
                    INSERT INTO serviceinfos

                    """,
                    (
                        device_id,
                        doc_choice,
                        file.name,
                        save_path,
                        datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
                        title.strip() or None,

                conn.commit()

            # Upload-Counter hochzählen, damit nächster Upload einen neuen Key bekommt
            st.session_state.upload_counter[device_id] += 1

محدودیت: مطابق مستندات و مسائل موجود در مرجع‌ها، ویجت `file_uploader` فقط یک فایل را هر بار آپلود می‌کند و فایل‌ها در RAM نگهداری می‌شوند. حذف فایل از ویجت معمولاً باعث آزاد شدن حافظه می‌شود اما به نظر می‌رسد پاکسازی کامل در حالت معمول انجام نمی‌شود. همچنین دوبار اجرا شدن callback هنگام آپلود فایل جدید می‌تواند باعث مصرف حافظه بالاتر و باقی ماندن فایل‌ها در RAM شود. نیاز به جزئیات بیشتر درباره پیاده‌سازی داخلی و تعامل با حافظه است تا بتوان علت دقیق را تعیین کرد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: فایل‌های آپلود شده در RAM باقی می‌مانند به دلیل رفتار طبیعی ویجت `st.file_uploader` که فایل‌ها را نگهداری می‌کند تا امکان دسترسی به آنها در جلسات بعد وجود داشته باشد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: امکان پاک شدن برنامه‌ریزی شده ویجت فایل آپلودر وجود ندارد و نیازمند مکانیزم دیگری برای آزادسازی حافظه است.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: دوبار اجرا شدن callback هنگام آپلود مجدد فایل ممکن است به دلیل مکانیزم داخلی تغییر فایل در ویجت باشد که باعث افزایش مصرف حافظه می‌شود.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

Streamlit Version 1.49.1
Python Version 3.13.7

I searched for the issue on all known databases without success

I am facing the following issue with st.file_uploader:

When I am uploading a File about 600MB the RAM usage is after I selected the File about 660 MB.
At the moment I pressed the upload button the RAM usage increases up to 1800MB.
After the Upload is done, the RAM usage stays at 660MB.
If I close the browsertab it stays at 660MB, only when I close the streamlit instance the RAM gets free.

I tryed several solutions:

clear_on_submit=True
working with session state keys
gc.collect()
st.rerun()

If I set the clear_on_submit=false and deactivate the st.rerun() I am able to delete the File in the Widget and only then the file gets deleted from the RAM.

Please note that file uploader is a **bit problematic** because
- You can only upload one file at the time.

file uploader widget programmatically.

- You can only upload one file at the time.

sources.quote:
Please note that file uploader is a **bit problematic** because
- You can only upload one file at the time.
- You get no additional information on the file like name, size, upload time, type etc. So you
cannot distinguish the files without reading the content.
- every time you interact with any widget, the script is rerun and you risk processing or storing
the file again!
- The file uploader widget is not cleared when you clear the cache and there is no way to clear the
file uploader widget programmatically.

On each subsequent upload after the first upload, the `on_change` callback is called twice. My understanding is that uploading a new file also clears the existing file, triggering another callback execution. In that sense, this behavior might be a feature, not a bug. Nonetheless, this behavior can be confusing and unintuitive.

متن شاهد:

```text
Our incident: a `data=callable` on `st.download_button` called into functions that (transitively) read `@st.cache_data`-cached helpers. Because those calls run outside `ScriptRunContext`, they picked up cached results from a *different* request context — users occasionally downloaded a file that didn't match what they'd just generated on screen, with nothing in the logs to explain why. محدودیت: مطابق با گزارش‌های مرتبط، خطای UnserializableReturnValueError در استفاده از `@st.cache_data` هنگام برگرداندن نمونه‌های کلاس‌های سفارشی به دلیل ناسازگاری هویت کلاس‌ها رخ می‌دهد که ناشی از حذف و بارگذاری مجدد ماژول‌ها در `sys.modules` توسط LocalSourcesWatcher است. این موضوع منجر به تضاد بین کلاس‌های پیکربندی شده و نمونه‌های در حال پیکله شدن می‌شود که منجر به این خطا می‌گردد. بنابراین به نظر می‌رسد مشکل اصلی از تغییر و حذف نادرست ماژول‌ها در زمان اجرا است.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: خطا UnserializableReturnValueError ممکن است به دلیل ناسازگاری هویت کلاس به خاطر پاک شدن ماژول‌ها در sys.modules رخ دهد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: مشکل به علت حذف ناگهانی ماژول‌ها توسط LocalSourcesWatcher ایجاد می‌شود و منجر به تطابق نداشتن اشیاء در حافظه می‌شود.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: استفاده از کلاس‌های تعریف شده در ماژول‌هایی که در طول اجرا چندبار بارگذاری مجدد می‌شوند می‌تواند باعث بروز این خطا شود.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

summary.problem:
st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`


"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value


### `repro_agent.py`


"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.
"""
import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    import time
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42)


### `repro.py` — run with `streamlit run repro.py`


import streamlit as st
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py


st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"):
    # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does:
    #   for wm in self._watched_modules.values():
    #       del sys.modules[wm.module_name]
    if "repro_model" in sys.modules:
        del sys.modules["repro_model"]

    # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules
    importlib.import_module("repro_model")

    # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again
    repro_agent.get_result.clear()

    try:
        # rep

sources.quote:
- **#12069** — [st.empty does not clear removed elements](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12069): Very likely a duplicate. Reports the same core behavior where `st.empty()` containers fail to clear old elements if new content has fewer items, leaving ghost elements visible. Confirmed bug, P3.
- **#10126** — [`st.close()` or `st.end()` to remove stale elements mid-run](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10126): A feature request that directly addresses the underlying limitation. Proposes a mechanism to explicitly discard remaining stale elements within a container before the script run finishes, which would solve this issue.

Confirming this from a production incident — and it's a bit worse than "missing ScriptRunContext produces a warning": inside that thread, `st.session_state` reads return stale values and `@st.cache_data`-wrapped calls silently return whatever was already cached, **with no error and no warning**. Both just look like they worked.

Our incident: a `data=callable` on `st.download_button` called into functions that (transitively) read `@st.cache_data`-cached helpers. Because those calls run outside `ScriptRunContext`, they picked up cached results from a *different* request context — users occasionally downloaded a file that didn't match what they'd just generated on screen, with nothing in the logs to explain why. We only found the mechanism by tracing the full call graph of the callable, not just inspecting it — a lambda that looks pure can still be unsafe if anything it calls touches cached/session state indirectly.

sources.quote:
- **#12069** — [st.empty does not clear removed elements](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12069): Very likely a duplicate. Reports the same core behavior where `st.empty()` containers fail to clear old elements if new content has fewer items, leaving ghost elements visible. Confirmed bug, P3.
- **#10126** — [`st.close()` or `st.end()` to remove stale elements mid-run](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10126): A feature request that directly addresses the underlying limitation. Proposes a mechanism to explicitly discard remaining stale elements within a container before the script run finishes, which would solve this issue.

Confirming this from a production incident — and it's a bit worse than "missing ScriptRunContext produces a warning": inside that thread, `st.session_state` reads return stale values and `@st.cache_data`-wrapped calls silently return whatever was already cached, **with no error and no warning**. Both just look like they worked.

Our incident: a `data=callable` on `st.download_button` called into functions that (transitively) read `@st.cache_data`-cached helpers. Because those calls run outside `ScriptRunContext`, they picked up cached results from a *different* request context — users occasionally downloaded a file that didn't match what they'd just generated on screen, with nothing in the logs to explain why. We only found the mechanism by tracing the full call graph of the callable, not just inspecting it — a lambda that looks pure can still be unsafe if anything it calls touches cached/session state indirectly.

- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`


"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value


### `repro_agent.py`


"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.
"""
import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    import time
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42)


### `repro.py` — run with `streamlit run repro.py`


import streamlit as st
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py


st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")

        self.value = value

Helper module imported once by repro.py.

after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.

import streamlit as st
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py


st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"):
    # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does:
    #   for wm in self._watched_modules.values():
    #       del sys.modules[wm.module_name]
    if "repro_model" in sys.modules:
        del sys.modules["repro_model"]

    # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules
    importlib.import_module("repro_model")

    # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again
    repro_agent.get_result.clear()

    try:
        # repro_agent still uses the OLD MyResult class.
        # pickle resolves sys.modules["repro_model"].MyResult → NEW class.
        # OLD is not NEW → PicklingError → UnserializableReturnValueError
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

**Steps:**
1. `streamlit run repro.py`
2. Click **"1) Normal call"** — succeeds.
3. Click **"2) Simulate file-watcher"** — fails with `UnserializableReturnValueError`.
4. Click **"1) Normal call"** again — **also fails**, until Streamlit is restarted.


### Expected Behavior

Step 4 demonstrates persistence: `repro_agent` is never re-imported, so it keeps
using the old class, while `sys.modules` keeps the new one.

Neither step 3 not step 4 should throw the `UnserializableReturnValueError`.

Expected behavior :

### Current Behavior

`UnserializableReturnValueError` is thrown

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit**: 1.55.0
- **Python**: 3.13.7
- **OS**: Windows 11 / Linux (Kubernetes)
- Occurs more frequently in local dev (active filesystem) than in deployed containers

### Additional Information

> **Disclosure**: This bug report was written by an LLM (Claude) after a deep investigation into a production issue. The root cause analysis, reproduction script, and identified problematic code path are all LLM-generated

## Suggested Fixes

### Option A: Chain the original exception (low-effort, improves DX)

In `_handle_cache_miss`, chain the original exception so users can see the real error:

```python
raise UnserializableReturnValueError(
    return_value=computed_value, func=self._info.func
) from ex  # <-- add "from ex"
```

### Option B: Guard `write_result` against stale class references

Before calling `pickle.dumps()` in `DataCache.write_result`, re-import the module and verify class identity:

```python
import importlib
cls = type(value)
mod = sys.modules.get(cls.__module__)
if mod is not None:
    current_cls = getattr(mod, cls.__qualname__, None)
    if current_cls is not None and current_cls is not cls:
        # Module was reloaded — update the instance's class to the current one
        value.__class__ = current_cls
```

### Option C: Don't delete modules from `sys.modules` preemptively

Instead of deleting all watched modules on every file change, only invalidate the module that actually changed. Or defer the deletion to the start of the next script run rather than doing it immediately from the watcher thread.

## Workaround

Return only pickle-safe primitives (dicts, strings, numbers) from `@st.cache_data` functions, and reconstruct custom objects outside the cache boundary:

```python
@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def _cached_call(key: str) -> dict:
    result = do_expensive_work(key)
    return result.__dict__  # dict is always pickle-safe

def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    return MyResult(**_cached_call(key))
```

- **#12069** — [st.empty does not clear removed elements](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12069): Very likely a duplicate. Proposes a mechanism to explicitly discard remaining stale elements within a container before the script run finishes, which would solve this issue.

Confirming this from a production incident — and it's a bit worse than "missing ScriptRunContext produces a warning": inside that thread, `st.session_state` reads return stale values and `@st.cache_data`-wrapped calls silently return whatever was already cached, **with no error and no warning**. summary.problem:
Unexpected Page Refresh and Lost Selection in Streamlit 1.24.0 when using image_select

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I encountered an issue with Streamlit version 1.24.0 where the page would refresh entirely, causing the loss of the selected item when using the image_select function. However, the problem was not present in Streamlit version 1.22.0. As a workaround, I am currently using Streamlit 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.

Steps to Reproduce:

Upgrade Streamlit to version 1.24.0.
Implement an app that includes the image_select function.
Run the app and observe the behavior when using image_select to select an item.
Notice that upon selection, the entire page refreshes, leading to the loss of the selected item.
Expected Behavior:
When using image_select, the selection should be retained without causing the page to refresh entirely (session states should keep the current selection active)

Actual Behavior:
In Streamlit version 1.24.0, the page refreshes entirely, resulting in the loss of the selected item.

Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.24.0
Not Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.22.0
Additional Notes:

The issue specifically affects Streamlit version 1.24.0, but it was not present in version 1.22.0.
The unexpected page refresh and lost selection occur specifically when using the image_select function.
As a temporary workaround, I am using Streamlit version 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.
This behavior significantly impacts user experience, as it prevents the proper selection of items within the app.
Environment:

Operating System: [Win 11]
Python version: [3.10]
Streamlit version: 1.24.0
This issue is submitted to report the unexpected page refresh and lost selection problem that occurs when using the image_select function in Streamlit version 1.24.0. The problem was not observed in Streamlit version 1.22.0, and for the time being, I am using that version as a workaround. It would be helpful to investigate and address this behavior to ensure the smooth functioning of applications using image_select.

summary.problem:
Unexpected Page Refresh and Lost Selection in Streamlit 1.24.0 when using image_select

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I encountered an issue with Streamlit version 1.24.0 where the page would refresh entirely, causing the loss of the selected item when using the image_select function. However, the problem was not present in Streamlit version 1.22.0. As a workaround, I am currently using Streamlit 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.

Steps to Reproduce:

Upgrade Streamlit to version 1.24.0.
Implement an app that includes the image_select function.
Run the app and observe the behavior when using image_select to select an item.
Notice that upon selection, the entire page refreshes, leading to the loss of the selected item.
Expected Behavior:
When using image_select, the selection should be retained without causing the page to refresh entirely (session states should keep the current selection active)

Actual Behavior:
In Streamlit version 1.24.0, the page refreshes entirely, resulting in the loss of the selected item.

Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.24.0
Not Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.22.0
Additional Notes:

The issue specifically affects Streamlit version 1.24.0, but it was not present in version 1.22.0.
The unexpected page refresh and lost selection occur specifically when using the image_select function.
As a temporary workaround, I am using Streamlit version 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.
This behavior significantly impacts user experience, as it prevents the proper selection of items within the app.
Environment:

Operating System: [Win 11]
Python version: [3.10]
Streamlit version: 1.24.0
This issue is submitted to report the unexpected page refresh and lost selection problem that occurs when using the image_select function in Streamlit version 1.24.0. The problem was not observed in Streamlit version 1.22.0, and for the time being, I am using that version as a workaround. It would be helpful to investigate and address this behavior to ensure the smooth functioning of applications using image_select.

payload.message:
Unexpected Page Refresh and Lost Selection in Streamlit 1.24.0 when using image_select

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I encountered an issue with Streamlit version 1.24.0 where the page would refresh entirely, causing the loss of the selected item when using the image_select function. However, the problem was not present in Streamlit version 1.22.0. As a workaround, I am currently using Streamlit 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.

Steps to Reproduce:

Upgrade Streamlit to version 1.24.0.
Implement an app that includes the image_select function.
Run the app and observe the behavior when using image_select to select an item.
Notice that upon selection, the entire page refreshes, leading to the loss of the selected item.
Expected Behavior:
When using image_select, the selection should be retained without causing the page to refresh entirely (session states should keep the current selection active)

Actual Behavior:
In Streamlit version 1.24.0, the page refreshes entirely, resulting in the loss of the selected item.

Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.24.0
Not Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.22.0
Additional Notes:

The issue specifically affects Streamlit version 1.24.0, but it was not present in version 1.22.0.
The unexpected page refresh and lost selection occur specifically when using the image_select function.
As a temporary workaround, I am using Streamlit version 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.
This behavior significantly impacts user experience, as it prevents the proper selection of items within the app.
Environment:

Operating System: [Win 11]
Python version: [3.10]
Streamlit version: 1.24.0
This issue is submitted to report the unexpected page refresh and lost selection problem that occurs when using the image_select function in Streamlit version 1.24.0. The problem was not observed in Streamlit version 1.22.0, and for the time being, I am using that version as a workaround. It would be helpful to investigate and address this behavior to ensure the smooth functioning of applications using image_select.

summary.problem:
Unexpected Page Refresh and Lost Selection in Streamlit 1.24.0 when using image_select

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I encountered an issue with Streamlit version 1.24.0 where the page would refresh entirely, causing the loss of the selected item when using the image_select function. However, the problem was not present in Streamlit version 1.22.0. As a workaround, I am currently using Streamlit 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.

Steps to Reproduce:

Upgrade Streamlit to version 1.24.0.
Implement an app that includes the image_select function.
Run the app and observe the behavior when using image_select to select an item.
Notice that upon selection, the entire page refreshes, leading to the loss of the selected item.
Expected Behavior:
When using image_select, the selection should be retained without causing the page to refresh entirely (session states should keep the current selection active)

Actual Behavior:
In Streamlit version 1.24.0, the page refreshes entirely, resulting in the loss of the selected item.

Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.24.0
Not Reproduced On:

Streamlit version 1.22.0
Additional Notes:

The issue specifically affects Streamlit version 1.24.0, but it was not present in version 1.22.0.
The unexpected page refresh and lost selection occur specifically when using the image_select function.
As a temporary workaround, I am using Streamlit version 1.22.0 to avoid the issue.
This behavior significantly impacts user experience, as it prevents the proper selection of items within the app.
Environment:

Operating System: [Win 11]
Python version: [3.10]
Streamlit version: 1.24.0
This issue is submitted to report the unexpected page refresh and lost selection problem that occurs when using the image_select function in Streamlit version 1.24.0. The problem was not observed in Streamlit version 1.22.0, and for the time being, I am using that version as a workaround. It would be helpful to investigate and address this behavior to ensure the smooth functioning of applications using image_select.

AxiosError: timeout exceeded - Streamlit file uploader

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`AxiosError: timeout exceeded` happens when uploading a CSV file to the file uploader widget. This error happens in my app hosted on both localhost and the Streamlit community cloud. It happens when I use a different browser and different CSV files too. Doesn't work when I disabled XsrfProtection in `config.toml` either. I tried disabling like this:
``
[server]
enableXsrfProtection = false
``

I tried making a new app from scratch with a new Python environment (3.11), that only has one Streamlit file uploader, but the same error happened. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.file_uploader("Upload a file")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start the app on localhost 
2. Upload a csv file, for example, the one attached here
[case2lignin.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18127875/case2lignin.csv)


### Expected Behavior

 The csv file is successfully uploaded. 

### Current Behavior

`AxiosError: timeout exceeded` happens and the file is not uploaded. 

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:  1.41.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: MacOS Sequoia 15.1
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

summary.problem:
AxiosError: timeout exceeded - Streamlit file uploader

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

`AxiosError: timeout exceeded` happens when uploading a CSV file to the file uploader widget. This error happens in my app hosted on both localhost and the Streamlit community cloud. It happens when I use a different browser and different CSV files too. Doesn't work when I disabled XsrfProtection in `config.toml` either. I tried disabling like this:
``
[server]
enableXsrfProtection = false
``

I tried making a new app from scratch with a new Python environment (3.11), that only has one Streamlit file uploader, but the same error happened. 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.file_uploader("Upload a file")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start the app on localhost 
2. Upload a csv file, for example, the one attached here
[case2lignin.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18127875/case2lignin.csv)


### Expected Behavior

 The csv file is successfully uploaded. 

### Current Behavior

`AxiosError: timeout exceeded` happens and the file is not uploaded. 

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:  1.41.0
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: MacOS Sequoia 15.1
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

turns.response:
پاسخ پیشنهادی: از اسناد رسمی Streamlit پیروی کنید و در صورت نیاز برای ویژگی‌های خاص مانند به‌روزرسانی وضعیت در کَش، راهکارهای جایگزین بررسی کنید.

شاهد مستند: متن رسمی؛ سازگاری نسخه باید بررسی شود.

بخش منبع:

```text
Static elements
```

نسخهٔ منبع:

```text
695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd
```

متن شاهد:

```text
As we know, Streamlit only runs this function if it hasn’t been cached before. On this first run, the `st.success` message will appear in the app. But what happens on subsequent runs? It still shows up! Streamlit realizes that there is an `st.` command inside the cached function, saves it during the first run, and replays it on subsequent runs. Replaying static elements works for both caching decorators.
```

نشانی منبع:

```text
https://github.com/streamlit/docs/blob/695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd/content/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/cache-data.md
```

محدودیت: بر اساس مستندات رسمی، `st.cache_data` فرمان‌های Streamlit را در اجرای اولیه ذخیره می‌کند و در اجرای‌های بعدی پخش می‌کند، ولی توضیحی ندارد که همه فرمان‌ها به خصوص `status.update()` حتماً پخش می‌شوند و مشکل گزارش شده این امکان را می‌رساند که همه به‌روزرسانی‌ها همیشه بازتولید نمی‌شوند.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: عملکرد `st.cache_data` اغلب قادر به پخش مجدد فرمان‌های `st.` ذخیره‌شده در اجرای اولیه است، اما ممکن است برخی فرمان‌ها مانند `status.update()` به درستی پخش نشوند.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

summary.problem:
`st.cache_data` can't replay `st.status.update()` effect

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The `.update()` call of status container can't be replayed inside a cached function with `st.cache_data`, resulting in the status stuck with the init content.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st
@st.cache_data
def show_data():
    with st.status("Downloading data...", expanded=True) as status:
        st.write("Searching for data...")
        time.sleep(2)
        st.write("Found URL.")
        time.sleep(1)
        st.write("Downloading data...")
        time.sleep(1)
        status.update(
            label="Download complete!", state="complete", expanded=False
        )

show_data()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

use status container inside a cached function with st.cache_data, then call status.update

### Expected Behavior

When reruning the cached function, the status container should replay the "Download complete!" update after the st.write effects.

### Current Behavior

the status container replays only the st.write effects, but stuck in "Downloading data..." because the last update is not replayed:
[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.40.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

sources.quote: As we know, Streamlit only runs this function if it hasn’t been cached before. On this first run, the `st.success` message will appear in the app. But what happens on subsequent runs? It still shows up! Streamlit realizes that there is an `st.` command inside the cached function, saves it during the first run, and replays it on subsequent runs. Replaying static elements works for both caching decorators.

`st.cache_data` can't replay `st.status.update()` effect

### Checklist

- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The `.update()` call of status container can't be replayed inside a cached function with `st.cache_data`, resulting in the status stuck with the init content.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st
@st.cache_data
def show_data():
    with st.status("Downloading data...", expanded=True) as status:
        st.write("Searching for data...")
        time.sleep(2)
        st.write("Found URL.")
        time.sleep(1)
        st.write("Downloading data...")
        time.sleep(1)
        status.update(
            label="Download complete!", state="complete", expanded=False
        )

show_data()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

use status container inside a cached function with st.cache_data, then call status.update

### Expected Behavior

When reruning the cached function, the status container should replay the "Download complete!" update after the st.write effects.

### Current Behavior

the status container replays only the st.write effects, but stuck in "Downloading data..." because the last update is not replayed:
[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.40.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Chrome

_No response_

payload.message:
`st.cache_data` can't replay `st.status.update()` effect

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The `.update()` call of status container can't be replayed inside a cached function with `st.cache_data`, resulting in the status stuck with the init content.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st
@st.cache_data
def show_data():
    with st.status("Downloading data...", expanded=True) as status:
        st.write("Searching for data...")
        time.sleep(2)
        st.write("Found URL.")
        time.sleep(1)
        st.write("Downloading data...")
        time.sleep(1)
        status.update(
            label="Download complete!", state="complete", expanded=False
        )

show_data()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

use status container inside a cached function with st.cache_data, then call status.update

### Expected Behavior

When reruning the cached function, the status container should replay the "Download complete!" update after the st.write effects.

### Current Behavior

the status container replays only the st.write effects, but stuck in "Downloading data..." because the last update is not replayed:
[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.40.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

actions.body:
پاسخ پیشنهادی: از اسناد رسمی Streamlit پیروی کنید و در صورت نیاز برای ویژگی‌های خاص مانند به‌روزرسانی وضعیت در کَش، راهکارهای جایگزین بررسی کنید.

شاهد مستند: متن رسمی؛ سازگاری نسخه باید بررسی شود.

بخش منبع:

```text
Static elements
```

نسخهٔ منبع:

```text
695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd
```

متن شاهد:

```text
As we know, Streamlit only runs this function if it hasn’t been cached before. On this first run, the `st.success` message will appear in the app. But what happens on subsequent runs? It still shows up! Streamlit realizes that there is an `st.` command inside the cached function, saves it during the first run, and replays it on subsequent runs. Replaying static elements works for both caching decorators.
```

نشانی منبع:

```text
https://github.com/streamlit/docs/blob/695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd/content/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/cache-data.md
```

محدودیت: بر اساس مستندات رسمی، `st.cache_data` فرمان‌های Streamlit را در اجرای اولیه ذخیره می‌کند و در اجرای‌های بعدی پخش می‌کند، ولی توضیحی ندارد که همه فرمان‌ها به خصوص `status.update()` حتماً پخش می‌شوند و مشکل گزارش شده این امکان را می‌رساند که همه به‌روزرسانی‌ها همیشه بازتولید نمی‌شوند.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: عملکرد `st.cache_data` اغلب قادر به پخش مجدد فرمان‌های `st.` ذخیره‌شده در اجرای اولیه است، اما ممکن است برخی فرمان‌ها مانند `status.update()` به درستی پخش نشوند.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

actions.body:
پاسخ پیشنهادی: مطالعه دقیق‌تر مستندات رسمی Streamlit درباره رفتار بازپخش دستورات استریم‌لیت داخل توابع کش شده و بررسی اینکه آیا پشتیبانی از `st.status.update()` ذکر شده است یا خیر.

شاهد مستند: متن رسمی؛ سازگاری نسخه باید بررسی شود.

بخش منبع:

```text
Static elements
```

نسخهٔ منبع:

```text
695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd
```

متن شاهد:

```text
As we know, Streamlit only runs this function if it hasn’t been cached before. On this first run, the `st.success` message will appear in the app. But what happens on subsequent runs? It still shows up! Streamlit realizes that there is an `st.` command inside the cached function, saves it during the first run, and replays it on subsequent runs. Replaying static elements works for both caching decorators.
```

نشانی منبع:

```text
https://github.com/streamlit/docs/blob/695e6ce2fb1b23afc6df66b40420ab0013ad72fd/content/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/cache-data.md
```

محدودیت: با توجه به مستندات رسمی Streamlit، توابع کش شده توسط `st.cache_data` می‌توانند دستورات استریم‌لیت را اجرا کنند اما بازپخش دستورات استریم‌لیت در دفعات بعدی اجرا محدودیت‌هایی دارد. گزارش موجود از عدم بازپخش کامل `status.update` در توابع کش شده نشان می‌دهد که احتمال پشتیبانی آن محدود یا وجود ندارد، بنابراین مطالعه مستندات رسمی برای تایید دقیق این موضوع ضروری است.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: ممکن است `st.status.update()` داخل توابع کش‌شده توسط `st.cache_data` بازپخش نشود یا بازپخش آن محدود باشد.

summary.problem:
`st.cache_data` can't replay `st.status.update()` effect

### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The `.update()` call of status container can't be replayed inside a cached function with `st.cache_data`, resulting in the status stuck with the init content.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import time
import streamlit as st
@st.cache_data
def show_data():
    with st.status("Downloading data...", expanded=True) as status:
        st.write("Searching for data...")
        time.sleep(2)
        st.write("Found URL.")
        time.sleep(1)
        st.write("Downloading data...")
        time.sleep(1)
        status.update(
            label="Download complete!", state="complete", expanded=False
        )

show_data()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

use status container inside a cached function with st.cache_data, then call status.update

### Expected Behavior

When reruning the cached function, the status container should replay the "Download complete!" update after the st.write effects.

### Current Behavior

the status container replays only the st.write effects, but stuck in "Downloading data..." because the last update is not replayed:
[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.40.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_
